description:
Prefill/decode disaggregation. Everything here is specific to a PD deployment -- for a single-role model the panels are empty by construction, which is why this is its own dashboard rather than rows on the model dashboard.

Roles carry a real `role` label from the worker's metrics aggregator, not a pod-name regex, so nothing here breaks when instance naming changes or when an engine's role is not in its pod name.

panels.title: Is disaggregation actually happening — engine token accounting (vLLM: both NIXL and Mooncake)
panels.description: Read from the ENGINE rather than the connector, which is why it still works on Ascend/Mooncake where every transfer counter is missing. SGLang does not export `prompt_tokens_by_source`, so on SGLang only `Requests Routed` fills in here — see each panel's ⓘ.

panels.title: Decode Tokens From Transfer
panels.description:
How much of decode's prompt tokens arrived FROM prefill instead of being recomputed locally.

**This is the first thing to read**, because it comes from the engine rather than the connector: it still has data on Mooncake, which exports no transfer counters at all.

100% = every token reused prefill's work. Near 0% = disaggregation has silently collapsed into aggregated inference.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — yes · the one transfer signal Mooncake still gives you
- SGLang — no · `prompt_tokens_by_source` is not exported

Source: `gpustack:pd_prompt_tokens_by_source` ← `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source` (engine, not connector)

panels.title: Decode Tokens Recomputed
panels.description:
Prompt tokens decode computed itself. **A healthy group sits at 0.**

Anything else means KV did not arrive, or arrived late, and decode fell back to recomputing — the cost of disaggregation paid without the benefit.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — yes
- SGLang — no · same metric missing

Source: `gpustack:pd_prompt_tokens_by_source` ← `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source`

panels.title: Requests Routed
panels.description:
Counted at the router, which is the only place a request is counted ONCE. Engine-side request counters double under PD: every request traverses both roles, so summing them across the group reports twice the traffic.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — yes
- SGLang — yes

Source: `gpustack:pd_router_requests` ← `vllm_router_pd_requests` / `smg_router_requests`

panels.title: Prefill Cache Hit
panels.description:
Share of prefill's prompt tokens served from the prefix cache. Unrelated to PD, but it **erodes PD's payoff**: when prefix hits are high, prefill was cheap to begin with, so the compute disaggregation saves is worth less.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — yes
- SGLang — no · SGLang reports `cache_hit_rate`, which is not split by source

Source: `gpustack:pd_prompt_tokens_by_source` ← `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source`

panels.title: Prompt Tokens by Source
panels.description:
Prompt tokens per second, split by where they came from. A healthy group shows two lines that track each other: `prefill · local_compute` and `decode · external_kv_transfer`.

`decode · local_compute` rising is disaggregation degrading.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — yes
- SGLang — no

Source: `gpustack:pd_prompt_tokens_by_source` ← `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source`

panels.title: Requests Dispatched by Role
panels.description:
Per-worker dispatch counts from the router. The two lines diverging means requests are reaching one role and not the other.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — yes
- SGLang — no · its gateway exports the route aggregate only, with no per-worker dispatch counter

Source: `gpustack:pd_router_{prefill,decode}_requests` ← `vllm_router_pd_*_requests`

panels.title: Is the prefill:decode ratio right — engine metrics, every backend reports these
panels.description: vLLM+NIXL, vLLM+Mooncake (Ascend) and SGLang all export these. Empty here means nothing was running in this window.

panels.title: Queue Depth by Role
panels.description:
🔑 The only objective signal for whether the ratio is right, and which way it is wrong: a queue that only ever builds on one side is that side asking for more replicas.

Read the SHAPE, not the value -- a queue that drains is healthy at any depth.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — yes
- SGLang — yes

Source: `gpustack:num_requests_waiting` ← `vllm:num_requests_waiting` / `sglang:num_queue_reqs`

panels.title: Requests In Flight by Role
panels.description:
Concurrency actually achieved per role.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — yes
- SGLang — yes

Source: `gpustack:num_requests_running` ← `vllm:num_requests_running` / `sglang:num_running_reqs`

panels.title: Time To First Token by Role
panels.description:
🔑 TTFT belongs to PREFILL -- that is what a user waited for. Decode's TTFT is the time from its own first forward pass and is not comparable.

This is why the two are charted apart rather than averaged: a figure across both roles describes neither, which is the premise of running PD at all.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — yes
- SGLang — yes

Source: `gpustack:time_to_first_token_seconds` ← `vllm:` / `sglang:time_to_first_token_seconds`

targets.expr: sum by (role) (increase(gpustack:time_to_first_token_seconds_sum{cluster_name="$cluster_name", model_name="$model_name", role=~"$role"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (role) (increase(gpustack:time_to_first_token_seconds_count{cluster_name="$cluster_name", model_name="$model_name", role=~"$role"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Time Per Output Token by Role
panels.description:
🔑 TPOT belongs to DECODE. Prefill emits one token and then hands over, so its inter-token latency is not a steady-state figure.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — yes
- SGLang — yes

Source: `gpustack:time_per_output_token_seconds` ← `vllm:` / `sglang:time_per_output_token_seconds`

targets.expr: sum by (role) (increase(gpustack:time_per_output_token_seconds_sum{cluster_name="$cluster_name", model_name="$model_name", role=~"$role"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (role) (increase(gpustack:time_per_output_token_seconds_count{cluster_name="$cluster_name", model_name="$model_name", role=~"$role"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: KV transfer: how fast, how big, is any lost — ⚠️ connector-dependent: none on Mooncake, duration only on SGLang
panels.description:
⚠️ These read the **connector's own** counters, and connectors differ sharply:

- **vLLM + NIXL** — bytes, duration, failures, leases: all of it
- **vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend)** — none of it. `mooncake/stats.py` exports zero counters where NIXL exports fifteen; judge disaggregation from the token accounting in the first row instead
- **SGLang** — duration only (`kv_transfer_bootstrap_ms`); no bytes counter since 0.5.15

Whichever side `KV counted on` does not name reads zero forever (NIXL and Mooncake count on decode, SGLang on prefill).

panels.title: KV Transfer Mean
panels.description:
Mean time for one KV transfer (sum/count).

Mean rather than p99 here: ⚠️ **The percentiles saturate.** The engine's histogram tops out at a 5 s bucket, so when transfers are routinely slower than that — common cross-host without RDMA — p50, p95 and p99 all pin to 5. That is the bucket edge, not a measurement.

Measured on a cross-host NIXL run: 1888 of 1919 transfers landed in `+Inf`, all three percentiles read 5 s, and the true mean from sum/count was 115 s. **When they pin, read the `mean` series** — it is immune to bucketing.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — **no** · `mooncake/stats.py` exports zero counters where NIXL exports fifteen
- SGLang — yes · `kv_transfer_bootstrap_ms`, ms scaled to s

Source: `gpustack:pd_kv_transfer_seconds` ← `vllm:nixl_xfer_time_seconds` / `sglang:kv_transfer_bootstrap_ms`

panels.title: Bytes per Transfer
panels.description:
Mean transfer size. A drop here precedes a slowdown: smaller chunks pay the per-transfer overhead more often for the same volume.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — **no**
- SGLang — **no** · `kv_transfer_total_mb` was dropped in 0.5.15, nothing replaced it

Source: `gpustack:pd_kv_transfer_bytes` ← `vllm:nixl_bytes_transferred`

panels.title: KV Transfer Throughput
panels.description:
Bytes moved divided by time spent moving them -- throughput WHILE transferring, not per wall-clock second. Dividing by wall clock would make a mostly-idle window read as a collapse.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — **no**
- SGLang — **no** · needs the bytes counter SGLang no longer has

Source: `gpustack:pd_kv_transfer_bytes` ÷ `gpustack:pd_kv_transfer_seconds`

panels.title: KV Transfers per Request
panels.description:
🔴 The one signal that separates 'PD is working' from 'PD silently collapsed to aggregated serving'. Around 1.0 on a healthy pair. Near 0 while requests are still being routed means the deployment answers correctly, logs nothing, shows every instance Running -- and is not disaggregating at all.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — **no**
- SGLang — yes

Source: `gpustack:pd_kv_transfer_seconds_count` ÷ `gpustack:pd_router_requests`

panels.title: Failed Transfers
panels.description:
Cumulative. Any nonzero value is transfers that actually failed.

⚠️ **Blank is not zero.** This counter does not exist on every connector, so an empty tile means unmeasured — not healthy.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — **no**
- SGLang — **no**

Source: `gpustack:pd_kv_transfer_failed` ← `vllm:nixl_num_failed_transfers`

panels.title: KV Leases Expired
panels.description:
Requests dropped between the two hops: prefill computed their KV and nobody ever read it. Rising means work is being thrown away.

⚠️ **Blank is not zero.** This counter does not exist on every connector, so an empty tile means unmeasured — not healthy.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — **no**
- SGLang — **no**

Source: `gpustack:pd_kv_lease_expired` ← `vllm:nixl_num_kv_expired_reqs`

panels.title: KV Transfer Duration Percentiles
panels.description:
p99 lifting away from p50 is the transport degrading under load; all three rising together is the transfers getting bigger.

⚠️ **The percentiles saturate.** The engine's histogram tops out at a 5 s bucket, so when transfers are routinely slower than that — common cross-host without RDMA — p50, p95 and p99 all pin to 5. That is the bucket edge, not a measurement.

Measured on a cross-host NIXL run: 1888 of 1919 transfers landed in `+Inf`, all three percentiles read 5 s, and the true mean from sum/count was 115 s. **When they pin, read the `mean` series** — it is immune to bucketing.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — **no** · `mooncake/stats.py` exports zero counters
- SGLang — yes · `kv_transfer_bootstrap_ms`, ms scaled to s

Source: `gpustack:pd_kv_transfer_seconds` ← `vllm:nixl_xfer_time_seconds` / `sglang:kv_transfer_bootstrap_ms`

panels.title: KV Transfer Throughput over time
panels.description:
Judge this against its own history. A step down that persists is the transport falling back -- RDMA to TCP being the case worth catching.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — **no**
- SGLang — **no** · needs the bytes counter SGLang no longer has

Source: `gpustack:pd_kv_transfer_bytes` ÷ `gpustack:pd_kv_transfer_seconds`

panels.title: KV Transfers per Request over time
panels.description:
A step down to zero while traffic continues is the silent collapse. Gaps are windows with no traffic -- not zeros, which would read as 'KV stopped moving'.

**Where this has data**

- vLLM + NIXL — yes
- vLLM + Mooncake (Ascend) — **no**
- SGLang — yes

Source: `gpustack:pd_kv_transfer_seconds_count` ÷ `gpustack:pd_router_requests`

list.name: model_name
list.description: PD groups only. Sourced from `model_role_desired_instances`, which is derived from a model's roles, so aggregated deployments never appear here — pointing this dashboard at one used to produce nineteen empty panels. A stopped group still lists, because the metric comes from the spec rather than from traffic.

list.name: counted_role
list.label: KV counted on
list.description: Which side of a pair owns the KV transfer counters is a property of the connector, not a preference: NIXL PULLs so decode counts; SGLang PUSHes so prefill counts. The side you do not pick reads zero forever, and every transfer panel then shows an empty or zero value. Arriving from a model's Monitoring link sets this from the catalog; switching models by hand does not.

list.label: Roles
list.description: Which roles the per-role panels show.
